speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how many users of personal mobility devices (PMDs) and their accident victims have gone for mediation in the past 24 months; (b) what compensation has been paid out in the mediation; (c) what is the cost of mediation that each party must bear; (d) how long is the whole process of mediation; and (e) what is the process should one party refuse to attend.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Mediation is voluntary and can only proceed with both parties in attendance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The SMC facilitates this by contacting the relevant parties and explaining the benefits of mediation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: SMC also provides subsidised rates to applicants with financial difficulties on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The duration of mediation depends on the complexity of the issues and the parties’ willingness to resolve the dispute.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The negotiation process is confidential, and parties generally do not disclose the compensation amount.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: If mediation fails, either because one party refuses to attend or the parties are unable to come to a resolution, the claimant can choose to file a civil suit in the State Courts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Active Mobility Advisory Panel and the Land Transport Authority (LTA) strongly encourage all active mobility device users to purchase third-party liability insurance to protect themselves against third-party claims in the event of an accident.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned earlier that if one party refuses to attend mediation, then the next recourse is to file a civil suit.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: A lot of people think that, firstly, it costs money and it is very troublesome.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is there anything that the Ministry can do to make it easier?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If one party refuses to turn up, very likely that party is at fault.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Thirdly, how do we ensure that all these shared e-scooters do not pose a danger to pedestrians and cause disamenities and chaos like what shared bicycles have done previously?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: A lot of residents have already given the feedback why is it that we are opening up to these shared e-scooter operators.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned earlier that it is not compulsory, if I heard him correctly.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can we make it compulsory so that when it comes to claims, the injured person can claim against the insurance of the other party?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the first question on civil suit, like I have mentioned, if the two parties can agree on some form of mediation, that would be one of the best outcomes, failing which, the claimant can also consider a civil suit against the offender in the State Courts.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In a situation where the claimant is unable to afford the legal fees, the claimant can also approach the Legal Aid Bureau which offers help to those who have difficulty procuring legal representation on their own.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Of course, that would require some form of means-testing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition to that, the claimant can also approach the Law Society of Singapore which can provide ad hoc pro bono services, with free legal representation on a referred basis.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If the claimant wants to have some form of legal advice, they can also approach the community legal clinics at the Law Society as they do offer basic legal advice and give advice on the possible next course of action.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to e-scooter sharing licences, so far, we have received quite good responses.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I do not have the exact numbers of licences that would be issued.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But once that information is available, I will be able to share with the Member.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the third supplementary question on e-scooter safety, we have the benefit of learning from our bike-sharing experiences.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With the implementation of the Active Mobility Act and the implementation of safety requirements on PMD users, we will be able to ensure that the use of e-scooters will be done in a safe manner.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to third-party insurance, right now, it is not compulsory because the Active Mobility Advisory Panel did not recommend mandating this, given the diversity in device users, so as not to significantly reduce the uptake of active mobility.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For example, it can be quite onerous on occasional active mobility users as well as families and young children to purchase mandatory third-party insurance.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Instead, the Advisory Panel suggested placing greater focus on upstream prevention of accidents, such as lowering the speed limits on footpaths and, at the same time, encouraging users to stop and look out for oncoming traffic at road crossings.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, these are some of the measures that the Active Mobility Advisory Panel has suggested.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, having said that, the Panel strongly encourages the take-up of third-party liability insurance, in particular, by food delivery companies, for the employees.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, while it is not mandatory for PMD users to purchase third-party insurance, we do strongly encourage all active mobility device users to purchase third-party liability insurance to protect themselves against third-party claims in the event of an accident.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: For the pro bono legal advice provided by the Law Society, is it means-tested, that means, is it anybody can go and ask?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Because it is not easy to get help from Legal Aid.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, if everybody were to go along that direction, I think it is quite onerous, quite tough.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, perhaps if there are increasing complaints, increasing incidents, perhaps the Ministry should look into how best to address this.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: If the appropriate party did not turn up, that means that the other party is at fault.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, this is actually another avenue where victims can seek compensation.
